components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Primary action for checkout, saving, and decisive administrative work.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height:44px; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:16px; padding:12px 16px; border:1px solid #0b615a; border-radius:8px; background:#0f766e; color:#fff; font:750 12px/1.35 Inter, sans-serif; transition:background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(.25,1,.5,1), transform 50ms ease, box-shadow 50ms ease; box-shadow:0 2px 0 #084c47; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:#115e59; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #0f766e; outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform:translateY(2px); box-shadow:none; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Flat secondary action for supporting workflow choices.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { min-height:44px; padding:10px 14px; border:1px solid #c2c8d0; border-radius:6px; background:#f2f4f6; color:#111827; font:750 12px/1.35 Inter, sans-serif; transition:background-color 150ms ease, border-color 150ms ease, color 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color:#83aaa6; background:#dcece9; color:#115e59; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #0f766e; outline-offset:2px; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { background:#d7dce2; }

components.name: Tactile POS Key
components.description: Repeatedly pressed product, category, or numpad control.
components.css: .ds-tactile-key { width:72px; min-height:44px; padding:10px; border:1px solid #b9c2ca; border-radius:8px; background:#f2f4f6; color:#111827; font:800 16px/1 Inter, sans-serif; box-shadow:0 2px 0 #a5b0b9; transition:background-color 150ms ease, border-color 150ms ease, transform 50ms ease, box-shadow 50ms ease; } .ds-tactile-key:hover { border-color:#87a9a5; background:#e4eeec; color:#174f4a; } .ds-tactile-key:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #0f766e; outline-offset:2px; } .ds-tactile-key:active { transform:translateY(2px); box-shadow:none; }

components.name: Operational Input
components.description: Compact touch-friendly search and data-entry field.
components.css: .ds-field { display:grid; gap:6px; color:#4b5563; font:750 12px/1.35 Inter, sans-serif; } .ds-field input { min-width:240px; height:44px; padding:10px 12px; border:1px solid #c2c8d0; border-radius:6px; outline:0; background:#f2f4f6; color:#111827; font:500 14px/1.5 Inter, sans-serif; box-shadow:inset 0 1px 2px rgb(17 24 39 / 9%); } .ds-field input:focus { border-color:#0f766e; box-shadow:0 0 0 2px rgb(15 118 110 / 15%); } .ds-field input:disabled { opacity:.55; cursor:not-allowed; }

components.name: Selected State Chip
components.description: Restrained active-state label for filters and operational status.
components.css: .ds-state-chip { display:inline-flex; min-height:28px; align-items:center; padding:4px 8px; border:1px solid #83aaa6; border-radius:6px; background:#dcece9; color:#115e59; font:800 11px/1.35 Inter, sans-serif; }

components.name: POS Product Card
components.description: Compact product tile with stable price and tactile response.
components.css: .ds-product-card { width:130px; aspect-ratio:1; display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:6px; padding:10px; border:1px solid #b9c2ca; border-radius:8px; background:#f2f4f6; color:#111827; box-shadow:0 2px 0 #a5b0b9; transition:filter 150ms ease, transform 50ms ease, box-shadow 50ms ease; } .ds-product-card strong { font:800 13px/1.35 Inter, sans-serif; } .ds-product-card span { color:#115e59; font:850 12px/1.35 Inter, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; } .ds-product-card:hover { filter:brightness(.985); } .ds-product-card:focus-visible { outline:2px solid #0f766e; outline-offset:2px; } .ds-product-card:active { transform:translateY(2px); box-shadow:none; }

components.name: Administrative Card
components.description: Flat reading surface for metrics, reports, and settings.
components.css: .ds-admin-card { width:240px; display:grid; gap:7px; padding:16px; border:1px solid #e4e4e7; border-radius:12px; background:#fff; color:#09090b; } .ds-admin-card span { color:#71717a; font:750 12px/1.35 Inter, sans-serif; } .ds-admin-card strong { color:#0f766e; font:800 24px/1.2 Inter, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; } .ds-admin-card small { color:#71717a; font:500 11px/1.5 Inter, sans-serif; }

narrative.overview:
POSAPP should feel like a well-kept restaurant counter: calm enough to read under pressure, compact enough to keep the next action close, and dependable enough to disappear into the work. The voice is calm, operational, and direct. Familiar controls win over decorative novelty.

The terminal, administration, and reporting surfaces are contextual expressions of the same system. The POS terminal uses low-glare layered neutrals and shallow tactile feedback for frequently pressed controls. Administration stays flatter and quieter. Reports use ledger-like alignment and hierarchy so operational and financial numbers can be checked quickly.

The system explicitly rejects generic AI-style layouts, excessive rounding or padding, glare, gradients, decorative icons, heavy shadows, clutter, oversized cards, unnecessary motion, flicker, and unnatural interface copy.
keyCharacteristics: Restrained Service Teal used only for action, selection, and meaningful state
Low-glare POS surfaces with brighter administrative reading surfaces
Compact, tactile, dependable controls with clear focus and pressed states
Flat-by-default containers separated by tone and one-pixel borders
Arabic and English parity, logical RTL layout, and Latin tabular digits
Structural responsiveness for phones, tablets, POS touchscreens, and desktops

rules.name: The Teal Means Action Rule
rules.body: Service Teal marks a primary action, current selection, or meaningful live state. It is never background decoration.

rules.name: The Low-Glare Rule
rules.body: POS work areas use Low-Glare Steel and Work Surface instead of large pure-white fields. Administrative reports may use Paper White because reading density is the task.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Rose is destructive, amber is cautionary, and teal is affirmative. Never use these colors interchangeably.

rules.name: The One Operational Voice Rule
rules.body: Routine UI uses the body family. Space Grotesk is limited to large Latin dashboard data, and Arabic never inherits Latin display tracking.

rules.name: The Latin Digit Rule
rules.body: Digits remain Latin in Arabic and English. Monetary values, times, identifiers, and counts use tabular numerals while preserving the existing currency presentation.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards and panels rest flat. If a normal content card needs a large shadow to be understood, its border or tonal hierarchy is wrong.

rules.name: The Pressed-State Rule
rules.body: Tactile controls move down by two pixels and lose their edge shadow while pressed. They never bounce, scale, or glow.

dos: Do use Service Teal (#0f766e) for primary action, active selection, and meaningful operational state.
Do keep frequently pressed POS controls at least 44px high and give them a clear pressed state.
Do use low-glare POS surfaces and flatter administrative surfaces within the same component vocabulary.
Do use logical CSS properties, mirrored directional affordances, and natural Arabic translations.
Do keep Latin tabular digits for prices, times, identifiers, and counts in both languages.
Do adapt layouts structurally at phone, tablet, POS touchscreen, and desktop breakpoints.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion and keep ordinary state transitions between 150ms and 240ms.
Do make sensitive, destructive, and permission-controlled actions visually explicit without turning every action into a warning.
donts: Don't create generic AI-style layouts or unnatural interface copy.
Don't use excessive rounding, padding, glare, gradients, decorative icons, or heavy shadows.
Don't create clutter, oversized cards, or decoration that competes with operational information.
Don't add unnecessary motion, flicker, or transitions that slow down live service.
Don't introduce inconsistent controls or unfamiliar affordances without an operational reason.
Don't use Service Teal as decoration or apply saturated color to inactive states.
Don't shrink touch controls below practical use on phones, tablets, or dedicated POS hardware.
Don't apply uppercase letter spacing to Arabic or substitute Arabic numerals for Latin digits.
Don't use modal dialogs as the first solution when inline or progressive disclosure keeps the workflow clearer.
